```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(sfdep)
library(tmap)

#course data (read once for the whole page)
torn <- st_read("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1K5yFnDthJGKnWPragZPmQyCDpf8seSEI", quiet = TRUE)
nc_hosp <- st_read("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1K7lH1U6oQQ6sWXIqxOeFUYbWjdnxqx5a", quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_transform(2264)

#numbers quoted in the text below come from here, so they stay right if the data changes
fmt <- function(x, d = 0) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
```

## Part 1: Walkthrough {#walkthrough}

Run each chunk in your own .Rmd. You will reuse this code in Part 2.

### Step 1: Load the Data

::: {.why}
We'll use the touchdown points of `r fmt(nrow(torn))` U.S. tornadoes from 1954 to 2022, from [NOAA's Storm Prediction Center](https://www.spc.noaa.gov/gis/svrgis/). Useful columns are `yr` (year), `mag` (Enhanced Fujita rating), `inj` (injuries) and `fat` (fatalities). The data are already projected, so distances are in meters.
:::

```{r, eval = FALSE}
#load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(sfdep)
library(tmap)

#tornado touchdown points, 1954-2022
torn <- st_read("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1K5yFnDthJGKnWPragZPmQyCDpf8seSEI")
```

### Step 2: Mean Center

::: {.why}
The mean center is the average x coordinate and the average y coordinate of all the points.
:::

```{r}
torn_center <- center_mean(torn)

tm_shape(torn) + tm_dots(fill = "grey70") +
  tm_shape(torn_center) + tm_dots(fill = "blue", size = 1)
```

### Step 3: Weighted Mean Center

::: {.why}
A weighted mean center gives more pull to points with larger values of a variable. Weighting by fatalities moves the center toward the places where deadly tornadoes happen.
:::

```{r}
torn_center_fat <- center_mean(torn, weights = torn$fat)

tm_shape(torn) + tm_dots(fill = "grey70") +
  tm_shape(torn_center) + tm_dots(fill = "blue", size = 1) +
  tm_shape(torn_center_fat) + tm_dots(fill = "red", size = 1) +
  tm_add_legend(type = "symbols", labels = c("Mean center", "Weighted by fatalities"), fill = c("blue", "red"))

#how far apart are they? (meters, converted to miles)
st_distance(torn_center, torn_center_fat) / 1609.34
```

### Step 4: Standard Deviational Ellipse

::: {.why}
The standard deviational ellipse shows the spread of the points around the mean center and the direction they stretch in.
:::

```{r}
#calculate the ellipse values, then turn them into a shape
ellipse_vals <- std_dev_ellipse(torn)
torn_ellipse <- st_ellipse(geometry = ellipse_vals,
                           sx = ellipse_vals$sx,
                           sy = ellipse_vals$sy,
                           rotation = -ellipse_vals$theta)

tm_shape(torn) + tm_dots(fill = "grey70") +
  tm_shape(torn_ellipse) + tm_polygons(fill_alpha = 0.4)
```

## Part 2: Partner Practice {#partner-practice}

Both partners use the `r nrow(nc_hosp)` licensed hospitals in North Carolina, from [NC OneMap](https://www.nconemap.gov/datasets/hospitals). `hgenlic` is the number of general beds and `psylic` is the number of psychiatric beds. The data come in latitude and longitude, so project them to the NC State Plane system (in feet) first. Each task tells you in parentheses which walkthrough step to reuse.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
#NC hospitals, projected to NC State Plane (feet)
nc_hosp <- st_read("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1K7lH1U6oQQ6sWXIqxOeFUYbWjdnxqx5a") |>
  st_transform(2264)
```

:::: {.partners}
::: {.partner .partner-a}
### Partner A: General Beds

1. Find the mean center of all hospitals. *(Step 2)*
2. Find the mean center weighted by `hgenlic`, and the distance between the two centers in miles. Divide feet by 5,280. *(Step 3)*
3. Make the standard deviational ellipse for the hospitals that have general beds (`hgenlic > 0`). *(Step 4)*
4. Map the hospitals, both centers and the ellipse together.

When you finish, bring the distance between your two centers to Part 3, along with the city your weighted center is closest to and your map.
:::

::: {.partner .partner-b}
### Partner B: Psychiatric Beds

1. Count how many hospitals have any psychiatric beds.
2. Find the mean center weighted by `psylic`, and its distance in miles from the unweighted mean center. Divide feet by 5,280. *(Steps 2 and 3)*
3. Make the standard deviational ellipse for the hospitals that have psychiatric beds (`psylic > 0`). *(Step 4)*
4. Map the hospitals, both centers and the ellipse together.

When you finish, bring the count from item 1 and the distance between your two centers to Part 3, along with the city your weighted center is closest to and your map.
:::
::::

## Part 3: Together {#together}

1. Partner A finds the distance in miles between the general-bed center and the psychiatric-bed center with `st_distance()`.
2. Put your maps side by side and compare the two ellipses. Which kind of care is more spread out across the state?
3. North Carolina wants to fund one new psychiatric unit to improve access. Decide together which region it should go in, and why.

| Weighted by | Distance from the unweighted center (miles) | Closest city to the weighted center |
|---|---|---|
| General beds (Partner A) | | |
| Psychiatric beds (Partner B) | | |

::: {.deliver}
Each pair turns in one index card before leaving. Write both of your names on it, fill in the table, and add the distance between the two weighted centers. Then write two or three sentences saying where the new psychiatric unit should go and why.
:::

## Answer Key {#answer-key .answer-key}

```{r key-values, include = FALSE}
c_all <- center_mean(nc_hosp)
c_gen <- center_mean(nc_hosp, weights = nc_hosp$hgenlic)
c_psy <- center_mean(nc_hosp, weights = nc_hosp$psylic)
mi <- function(a, b) as.numeric(st_distance(a, b)) / 5280
d_gen <- mi(c_all, c_gen); d_psy <- mi(c_all, c_psy); d_gp <- mi(c_gen, c_psy)
n_psy <- sum(nc_hosp$psylic > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
e_gen <- std_dev_ellipse(filter(nc_hosp, hgenlic > 0))
e_psy <- std_dev_ellipse(filter(nc_hosp, psylic > 0))
#nearest hospital city to each weighted center, as a landmark
near_city <- function(pt) nc_hosp$fcity[st_nearest_feature(st_sf(geometry = pt), nc_hosp)]
city_gen <- near_city(c_gen); city_psy <- near_city(c_psy)
area_ratio <- (e_psy$sx * e_psy$sy) / (e_gen$sx * e_gen$sy)
```

| Item | General beds (A) | Psychiatric beds (B) |
|---|---|---|
| Hospitals with beds of this kind | `r sum(nc_hosp$hgenlic > 0, na.rm = TRUE)` | `r n_psy` |
| Distance from the unweighted center | `r fmt(d_gen, 1)` miles | `r fmt(d_psy, 1)` miles |
| Nearest hospital city to the weighted center | `r str_to_title(city_gen)` | `r str_to_title(city_psy)` |

The two weighted centers are `r fmt(d_gp, 1)` miles apart. The ellipse around hospitals with psychiatric beds covers `r fmt(100 * area_ratio)`% of the area of the ellipse around hospitals with general beds.

A good card says something like this. Only `r n_psy` of the `r nrow(nc_hosp)` hospitals have psychiatric beds, so that center depends on a few large hospitals. The ellipses show how evenly each kind of care is spread across the state. A new psychiatric unit should go where the psychiatric ellipse is thin compared with the general one, which means a region that has general hospitals but few psychiatric beds. The card should name that region and point to the maps as evidence.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
nc_hosp <- st_read("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1K7lH1U6oQQ6sWXIqxOeFUYbWjdnxqx5a") |>
  st_transform(2264)

#### Partner A: general beds ####
#A1: mean center (Step 2)
hosp_center <- center_mean(nc_hosp)

#A2: weighted by general beds, and distance in miles (Step 3)
gen_center <- center_mean(nc_hosp, weights = nc_hosp$hgenlic)
st_distance(hosp_center, gen_center) / 5280

#A3: ellipse for hospitals with general beds (Step 4)
gen_vals <- std_dev_ellipse(filter(nc_hosp, hgenlic > 0))
gen_ellipse <- st_ellipse(geometry = gen_vals, sx = gen_vals$sx, sy = gen_vals$sy,
                          rotation = -gen_vals$theta)

#A4: map
tm_shape(nc_hosp) + tm_dots(fill = "grey60") +
  tm_shape(gen_ellipse) + tm_polygons(fill = "orange", fill_alpha = 0.3) +
  tm_shape(hosp_center) + tm_dots(fill = "blue", size = 1) +
  tm_shape(gen_center) + tm_dots(fill = "orange", size = 1) +
  tm_add_legend(type = "symbols", labels = c("Mean center", "Weighted by general beds"),
                fill = c("blue", "orange"))

#### Partner B: psychiatric beds ####
#B1: hospitals with any psychiatric beds
sum(nc_hosp$psylic > 0)

#B2: weighted by psychiatric beds, and distance in miles (Steps 2 and 3)
hosp_center <- center_mean(nc_hosp)
psy_center <- center_mean(nc_hosp, weights = nc_hosp$psylic)
st_distance(hosp_center, psy_center) / 5280

#B3: ellipse for hospitals with psychiatric beds (Step 4)
psy_vals <- std_dev_ellipse(filter(nc_hosp, psylic > 0))
psy_ellipse <- st_ellipse(geometry = psy_vals, sx = psy_vals$sx, sy = psy_vals$sy,
                          rotation = -psy_vals$theta)

#B4: map
tm_shape(nc_hosp) + tm_dots(fill = "grey60") +
  tm_shape(psy_ellipse) + tm_polygons(fill = "purple", fill_alpha = 0.3) +
  tm_shape(hosp_center) + tm_dots(fill = "blue", size = 1) +
  tm_shape(psy_center) + tm_dots(fill = "purple", size = 1) +
  tm_add_legend(type = "symbols", labels = c("Mean center", "Weighted by psychiatric beds"),
                fill = c("blue", "purple"))

#### Part 3: together ####
st_distance(gen_center, psy_center) / 5280
```
